newsitem.title: SUDAN: Heads of state in Sudan to witness peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Heads of state in Sudan to witness peace deal.

text.p: Two African heads of state arrived in Sudan on Monday to see the government and rebel factions sign a peace deal which Khartoum hopes will help end a 14-year-old guerrilla war in the south.

State radio said Central African Republic President Ange-Felix Patasse and Chadian President Idriss Deby would attend the signing ceremony. Ministers from Chad and Malaysia will also be there, it added.

Four southern groups are signing the agreement but they do not include the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of Colonel John Garang, which does most of the fighting against the government and which has vowed to continue.
The southern groups expected to sign the agreement at 1530 GMT are splinter groups with few fighters on the ground. Most of them have been fighting the SPLA as pro-government militias.

Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter was quoted as saying in Sudan on Sunday that he and President Omar Hassan al-Bashir discussed the possibility of expanding the peace agreement to include other parties.
Carter also met Islamist leader Hassan al-Turabi for talks. He then left the capital on Sunday for the southern rebel-held town of Yei to meet Garang, U.S. officials said.
But in Nairobi, a rebel spokesman said on Monday a government warplane bombed Yei on Sunday, preventing Carter from landing there to meet a rebel leader.
Turabi, the speaker of parliament and ideological mentor to the Khartoum government, said Western countries had stopped Carter witnessing the signing of the peace agreement.
"The United States government...and Britain and the West prevented Carter from attending the ceremony tomorrow," he told state television on Sunday, adding Carter had wanted to attend.
